title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 43
paragraphs: Now this oracle, which Mardonius said referred to the Persians, I know for my part was composed with reference to the Illyrians and the army of the Enchelians, not to the Persians at all. However, the oracle composed by Bakis with reference to this battle —

“The gathering of Greeks together and cry of barbarian voices, where the Thermodon flows, by the banks of the grassy Asopos; here very many shall fall before destiny gave them to perish, bow-bearing Medes in fight, when the fatal day approaches them” —
these sayings, and others like them composed by Musaios, I know had reference to the Persians. Now the river Thermodon flows between Tanagra and Glisas.
